term: Exchange-Traded Fund: a basket of stocks or other assets that trades on an exchange like a single stock, often tracking an index.

copy.hook: How do you own 500 companies with just $100?
copy.explain: Put $100 into an S&P 500 ETF and you own a sliver of all 500 companies in one trade. If Apple is 7% of the fund, about $7 of your $100 rides on Apple.
copy.takeaway: One ticker, hundreds of companies: you buy the whole basket at once.
copy.question: If one stock in a 500-stock ETF drops 20%, does your ETF drop 20%? Why not?

chart.label: SPY
chart.why: The oldest US ETF, one share of the whole S&P 500
